topic.name: The Four Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix

question.text: Let $A$ and $B$ be $m \times p$ and $p \times n$ matrices, respectively. What is the image of $\text{Col}(B^T \! A^T)$ under the action of $AB?$
question.explanation:
Pre-multiplying a vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ by $AB$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $AB{:}$

\[ \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} \vert & \vert & \cdots & \vert \\ (ab)_1 & (ab)_2 & \cdots & (ab)_n \\ \vert & \vert & \cdots & \vert \end{bmatrix}}_{\large AB} \cdot \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ \vdots \\ x_n \end{bmatrix}}_{\large \mathbf{x}} = x_1 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ (ab)_1 \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ (ab)_2 \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} +\cdots+ x_n \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ (ab)_n \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} \]

Therefore, the image of $\mathbb{R}^n$ under the action of $AB$ must be $\text{Col}(AB),$ the column space of $AB.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}(AB)$ is mapped to the zero vector $\mathbf{0}$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}((AB)^T)=\text{Col}(B^T \! A^T)$ must be $\text{Col}(AB).$

question.text: Let $A$ and $B$ be $m \times n$ matrices. What is the image of $\text{Col}(A^T+B^T)$ under the action of $A+B?$
question.explanation:
Pre-multiplying a vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ by $A+B$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $A+B{:}$

\[ \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} \vert & \vert & \cdots & \vert \\ (a+b)_1 & (a+b)_2 & \cdots & (a+b)_n \\ \vert & \vert & \cdots & \vert \end{bmatrix}}_{\large A+B} \cdot \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ \vdots \\ x_n \end{bmatrix}}_{\large \mathbf{x}} = x_1 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ (a+b)_1 \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ (a+b)_2 \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} +\cdots+ x_n \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ (a+b)_n \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} \]

Therefore, the image of $\mathbb{R}^n$ under the action of $A+B$ must be $\text{Col}(A+B),$ the column space of $A+B.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}(A+B)$ is mapped to the zero vector $\mathbf{0}$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}((A+B)^T)=\text{Col}(A^T+B^T)$ must be $\text{Col}(A+B).$

example.title: Identifying the Images of the Four Fundamental Subspaces of the Matrix Under Its Action

The four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

In our case, we are given that $m=11,$ $n=7,$ and $m-r=6.$

Substituting $m=11$ into $m-r=6,$ we can find the rank of $A{:}$

\[ (11) - r = 6 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad r = 5 \]

Therefore, we obtain

\begin{align*} \text{dim}(\text{Col}(A)) &= r = 5. \end{align*}

In our case, we are given that $m=2,$ $n=4,$ and $m-r=1.$

Substituting $m=2$ into $m-r=1,$ we can find the rank of $A{:}$
